cd /home/nab-raj.roshyara@dg-nexolution.de/roshyara/personal/nrna1/docs/knowledgeos/knowlegeos_manual_theory_20261018/06-theory/manuscript; python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='chapter_01/CH-01-knowledge-authority-execution.md'; s=open(p).read()
a="Hence a further condition (Ded): an authority reference must resolve to an act **recorded before, and independently of,** the transaction that relies on it. The source proposes this as a new invariant (its OQ-33)."
b="Hence a further condition (Ded): an authority reference must resolve to an act **made and recorded by its human author, independently of the mechanism that relies on it**, never produced by that mechanism. Usually the act is recorded before the relying transaction. If it is recorded in the **same** atomic change, which §1.16.1 permits and even prefers, its record must show the human author, not the evaluator, as its source. The source proposes a narrower version of this as a new invariant (its OQ-33: \"not a value produced during the activating transaction\")."
assert s.count(a)==1; open(p,'w').write(s.replace(a,b))
p='BASELINE-REVISIONS.md'; t=open(p).read()
a="adds: the reference must resolve to an act recorded **before, and independently of,** the relying transaction"
b="adds: the reference must resolve to an act **made and recorded by its human author, independently of the relying mechanism** (usually before; if in the same atomic change, the record shows the human author). *Look-back correction: \"recorded before\" conflicted with §1.16.1's single atomic change*"
assert t.count(a)==1; open(p,'w').write(t.replace(a,b)); print('ok')
EOF
